shippingNews.postTitle: USCG Spar Towed to Fraser Shipyards

stories.body: Tug Nels J of Heritage/Dean Marine came down from its normal Two Harbors assignment Thursday to assist fleetmate and Superior-based tug Helen H in towing USCGC Spar from its base on Minnesota Point to Fraser Shipyards, where it will receive additional work after being idled this summer. Note: permission to fly within 3000 feet of SPAR was obtained in writing prior to drone flight. Spar under tow. [David Schauer] David Schauer

shippingNews.postTitle: Harriet M Joins Thunder Bay Tug Services Fleet

stories.body: A new tugboat has joined Thunder Bay Tug Services Ltd. with the arrival of Harriet M in Thunder Bay on October 8, 2026. The tug was acquired from Moran Towing Corporation of Philadelphia, PA. Built in 1978 at Jakobson Shipyard in Oyster Bay, NY, Harriet M measures approximately 28 metres in length and is powered by 3,005 horsepower. She will assist commercial vessels navigating the harbor and support ship movements throughout the Port of Thunder Bay as part of Thunder Bay Tug Services Ltd.’s operations, Michael Hull Harriet M arriving at the Port of Thunder Bay. todayInHistory.title: Sam Laud
todayInHistory.text: Sam Laud Bay Shipbuilding Corp. of Sturgeon Bay, WI, laid the keel for their hull # 712 on Jan. 4, 1974 to be built as a smaller-sized Great Lakes self-unloading bulk cargo carrier. The new vessel was launched on Nov. 19, 1974 for Buffalo's American Steamship Co. (ASC), a subsidiary of GATX Corp., Chicago, IL. Completed in 1975, the self-unloader was christened Sam Laud by Mrs. Edna Laud on behalf of her husband at a christening ceremony held April 15, 1975. Mr. Laud was the former president (1945) and chairman of the board (1956) of GATX Corp., having started with the company in 1916 as shop painter and riveter. Mr. Laud died August 1, 1963. GATX Corp. had acquired ASC in July of 1973. Mrs. Laud was accompanied by Mr. Frederick G. Jaicks, chairman and CEO of Inland Steel Co., Chicago, IL, who gave the address at the christening ceremonies. One of a new generation of self-unloaders for the ASC fleet, the Sam Laud was built at an approximate cost of $13.3 million and was the fourth of 10 self-unloaders launched for the fleet under Chapter XI of the Merchant Marine Act of 1970. Under this act, the U.S. government-guaranteed financing and tax deferred benefits for fleet modernizing. The other ASC self-unloaders built under this program were the Roger M. Kyes (now Adam E. Cornelius, 1973), Charles E. Wilson (now John J. Boland, 1973), H. Lee White (1974), St. Clair (1976), Belle River (now Walter J. marineWeather.synopsis: Lake Superior is currently between a 30.4 inch high over New York state and a 29.4 inch low over southern Saskatchewan, resulting in a tight pressure gradient and elevated winds today. A Gale Warning is in effect later today for portions of eastern Lake Superior. The low slowly weakens to 29.6 inches while tracking northeastward toward Ontario today into tonight. Meanwhile, 29.7 inch Hurricane Isaias will move north through Alabama, eventually helping to kick the high eastward off the Atlantic coast by early Sunday. Sunday morning, the Canada low will split into two weaker 29.7 inch lows, one settling over the Central Plains and one moving from northern Minnesota to northern Ontario. This will create weak 29.8 inch troughing over Lake Superior for Sunday, deepening to 29.7 inches by Monday evening. This is followed by pressure rises beginning late Tuesday, peaking at 30.3 inch high pressure settling over the Upper Great Lakes by Thursday.
marineWeather.warning: GALE WARNING IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE TONIGHT

marineWeather.synopsis: Low pressure around 29.2 inches over the Northern Plains will allow for southerly winds to gradually increase as it lifts northeastward. Southerly gusts up to 30 knots are expected starting this afternoon and continuing through early Sunday morning. A few gale force gusts are possible across the northern portions of the lake this afternoon and evening. Low pressure gradually weakens to 29.6 inches as it lifts into James Bay on Sunday, allowing winds to diminish. A cold front from the low will then progress through the Great Lakes Sunday night into Monday. This will allow for winds to veer gradually to northwesterly into Monday night, and northerly by Tuesday. Could see a few gale force gusts Monday night into Tuesday behind the cold frontal passage. Thunderstorms are possible along the front as well. Winds will gradually ease through the middle of the week as a high pressure system around 30.2 inches builds across the Upper Great Lakes region.

Remnants from Hurricane Isaias will work into way up into the Ohio Valley today and tomorrow, producing breezy southeast flow across the Great Lakes. This system, 29.80 inches, will center over the eastern Ohio River Valley tomorrow afternoon before exiting into New England Monday morning.

High pressure of 30.40 inches over the eastern Great Lakes will build to New England today. The remnant low of Isaias 29.80 inches will move northeast into the Ohio Valley Sunday and exit east off the Mid-Atlantic coast by Monday. A cold front with pressure of 29.70 inches will settle south across Lake Erie Tuesday afternoon. High pressure of 30.30 inches will build over the Upper Great Lakes on Wednesday.

A high pressure ridge averaging 30.1 inches exits slowly eastward today through Sunday before a weak trough averaging 29.8 inches slides eastward across the lake Sunday night. Behind the trough, a weak ridge averaging 29.9 inches slides eastward across the lake on Monday, exits eastward Monday night, and is followed by a cold front sweeping southeastward across the lake on Tuesday. Behind the cold front, a ridge averaging 30.0 inches builds from northern Ontario and vicinity through this Wednesday.
